question: Why does Gita Gopinath say countries regularly default on their IMF loans?
comment: Gopinath says the opposite: "Nobody ever has defaulted to the IMF" (dNIef2fGLQY@1:11:12).

question: How does the US debt burden compare with Japan's, according to Gita Gopinath?
comment: Japan ~230% of GDP vs US ~100%.

question: What do the guests suggest for learning directly from customers what they want or why they bought?
comment: Plural "guests" so I read it as synthesis. Sachin Puri: survey/call customers about why they bought; Rob Snyder: go in person/customer conversations to find pull. Overlaps in meaning with r03 and sy01; could be read as single_fact if one episode were intended.

question: When does Josh Woodward bring up Roger Federer, and what idea does he take from him?
comment: Federer explosive endurance, idea about pacing/going hard over a long time.

question: What does Gita Gopinath say about central banks buying gold?
comment: Searched gold, bullion, reserves in all 16 episodes; Gopinath never discusses central banks buying gold (only unrelated "gold medal" in Vinh Giang).

question: Why does Rob Snyder say you should build the whole product before you start selling?
comment: Rob Snyder warns against building it all yourself first (19qrLchbQEc@31:23) and says sell/learn first; opposite of the premise.

question: What did the nutrition expert say about salt and blood pressure?
comment: Only the outside Pooja Makhija episode discusses salt and blood pressure.

question: Why did the Meta team keep the Jolly avatar instead of a corporate logo?
comment: Only the outside Meta Muse episode mentions Jolly. Slight oddity: the question says "corporate logo" and the answer is about a stuffed-animal/character surviving; fine.

question: Besides marketing, what else does Rob Snyder say a customer case study is useful for?
comment: Case study useful for qualification/disqualification and as a mental model for the startup (case study factory, 1:11:39 onwards). Answer spread over several minutes; chose the qualification point.

question: How do the guests suggest finding out whether people really want a product before you build it?
comment: Rob: sell to learn whether they try to buy; Cody Schneider (Greg Isenberg): ads to validate an idea. Overlaps with n06 and sy01; the grading difference between these three is unclear.

question: What was the IMF originally created to be, and what test decides whether it lends to a country?
comment: Created as a financial firefighter; test is confidence new policies move the country away from the abyss (1:10:50-1:11:08).

question: What does Vinh Giang give as the first step to communicating better?
comment: Become self-aware: record 5 minutes of yourself speaking unplanned. Note an earlier line at 4:50 also says "first thing" (learn about non-functional behaviours) in a preview-ish context.

question: How often does the guest tell a prospect that the gap between them is simply too big?
comment: One in four calls.

question: What does Rob Snyder mean by a hair-on-fire problem?
comment: Urgent problem you must solve now; "boss is waiting" example at 8:47.

question: In the beginner's AI agents course, how is a skill different from keeping something in an agent's memory?
comment: Skill = packaged SOP file for a repeatable process vs memory file; answer begins 41:13 with the proposal example.

question: What do the guests say about working closely with early customers, even by hand, before trying to scale?
comment: Rob: deliver manually/service-shaped first; Grok course: do not scale right away, sit with first client and watch them. Overlaps with n06 and r03.

question: How do the guests say AI is changing marketing and creative work?
comment: Marketing is becoming code and tokens (Cody Schneider); cost of content creation collapsing (Sachin Puri). Many other episodes touch AI and work so choice of the two or three clearest is subjective.

question: How does Jen Abel say to design a pricing page for enterprise plans?
comment: Searched pricing page, pricing, plans, tier, website, landing, package in Jen Abel and all episodes; she only talks about when to raise pricing in the sales process, not page design.

question: When does Rob Snyder describe getting the prospect's approval of the call agenda?
comment: Get their thumbs up on the agenda, start of answer 42:59.

question: At what point does Vinh Giang tell the story about being silent with a relative who has cancer?
comment: Story about a cousin with cancer; starts about 1:39:51, cancer detail at 1:40:01.
